statement.title: A. Stair, Peak, or Neither?
statement.legend:
You are given three digits $a$, $b$, and $c$. Determine whether they form a stair, a peak, or neither.

 A stair satisfies the condition $a \lt b \lt c$.

 A peak satisfies the condition $a \lt b \gt c$.
statement.input_spec:
The first line contains a single integer $t$ ($1 \leq t \leq 1000$) — the number of test cases.

The only line of each test case contains three digits $a$, $b$, $c$ ($0 \leq a$, $b$, $c \leq 9$).
statement.output_spec: For each test case, output "STAIR" if the digits form a stair, "PEAK" if the digits form a peak, and "NONE" otherwise (output the strings without quotes).

samples.output:
STAIR
NONE
PEAK
PEAK
NONE
NONE
STAIR

editorial.tutorial: You just need to write two if-statements and check the two cases. Please note that some languages like C++ won't allow a chain of comparisons like a < b < c, and you should instead write it as a < b && b < c.
